newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Belarus warns Russia over visit snub to leader.
newsitem.headline: Belarus warns Russia over visit snub to leader.

text.p: The president of Belarus cancelled a visit to Russia's Kaliningrad region on Friday after the governor asked him to put it off due to concern over the arrest of a Russian television crew in Minsk, Russian media said.

The Belarus foreign ministry demanded an official explanation from Moscow of the snub, Itar-Tass news agency said. A spokesman for authoritarian Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko suggested Kremlin liberals were behind it.
The move marked a new chill in once warm relations between the former Soviet states following the arrests last weekend.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Lukashenko have exchanged harsh words. Yeltsin threatened to review the union treaty the two signed in May if the three journalists from Russian state-controlled ORT television were not freed.
Two of them face up to five years in jail after being charged with illegally crossing the Belarus-Lithuanian border.
International human rights groups have also urged their release and have criticised limits on press freedom in Belarus.
In Minsk on Thursday, 14 journalists who were taking part in and reporting on the handing in of a petition in support of the ORT crew were briefly detained.

Tass, Interfax and RIA news agencies quoted Lukashenko's spokesman in Minsk saying Friday's trip to the Baltic enclave of Kaliningrad was cancelled "due to an attempt by the Russians to link this visit to the ORT journalists' affair".

The spokesman said "pressure" from Moscow ran counter to international law and to the Russia-Belarus union treaty. Such attempts "seriously hinder the development of relations between Belarus and Russia as a whole and Kaliningrad region in particular", Interfax quoted the spokesman as saying.
Kaliningrad, sandwiched between Poland, Lithuania and the Baltic, is also cut off from the rest of Russia by Belarus.

Tass, reporting from Kaliningrad, said governor Leonid Gorbenko had sent a telegram overnight asking Lukashenko to come at a later date because of "concerns" relating to the "situation surrounding the arrest of the ORT journalists".
"It's obvious these actions...were not undertaken without participation by the opponents of Belarus-Russian integration in Moscow," Tass quoted Lukashenko's press service as saying.
Lukashenko on Thursday accused liberal First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais of trying to torpedo integration.

Liberals led by Chubais persuaded Yeltsin to water down the Belarus union treaty earlier this year. Kremlin sources said they feared the lack of market reforms in Belarus could hold Russia back and were concerned at giving Lukashenko a political platform in Russia.
Yeltsin said on Wednesday he was "surprised and indignant" at the arrests and suggested Moscow might revise the union.

Yeltsin's press secretary sought to calm the waters by saying Yeltsin did not want the incident to mar overall ties. But he added that Yeltsin wanted press freedoms to be maintained in both states in accordance with the union charter.

Detained ORT correspondent Pavel Sheremet had already been accused by the authorities of biased reporting and stripped of his press accreditation -- the second Russian television reporter to be punished in this way this year. Lukashenko said on Thursday Sheremet was in the pay of unnamed foreign powers.
Lukashenko rewrote the Belarus constitution in November last year after a landslide win in a referendum which critics said was illegitimate. The new basic law gives him vast powers.
